title: One Ticket, 800 Years
logline: Fixture: five scenes to exercise assets, timing and mix.
music_prompt: Warm, slow cinematic underscore for a documentary about Delhi: soft strings, bansuri flute, gentle tabla and a tanpura drone, about 70 BPM, wistful then hopeful, ending on a calm resolved chord.
cover_prompt: A golden metro train crossing an old Delhi skyline of Mughal domes at dusk, the Qutub Minar on the horizon, kites in a warm sky

scenes.narration: I am Dilli. <#0.5#> Buy one ticket for my Yellow Line, and I will carry you through eight hundred years.
scenes.image_prompt: Night view over the rooftops of Old Delhi with a glowing golden metro train curving through the city, lanterns and kites

scenes.narration: We board at Chandni Chowk. <#0.4#> In 1639, Shah Jahan began a walled city here, Shahjahanabad, with the Red Fort at its heart.
Further south lies Hauz Khas. Around 1295, Alauddin Khalji dug a great royal tank here to water his new city of Siri, and its stone steps still catch the evening light.
scenes.image_prompt: The great stone water tank of Hauz Khas at dusk, ruined domed pavilions and arches along its bank, reflections in still water, birds over the trees

scenes.narration: Personal memory removed at the maker’s request.
scenes.image_prompt: A small family with a tin trunk stepping off a bus into 1980s Delhi, seen from behind, warm evening light, a street food stall with steaming pans

scenes.narration: He made this film. <#0.5#> One ticket, eight hundred years, and I am still here, waiting for you at the next station.
scenes.image_prompt: A lone traveller seen from behind on an elevated metro platform at dawn, a golden train arriving, the silhouette of the Qutub Minar in the distance

claims.text: Shah Jahan began building Shahjahanabad in 1639.
Alauddin Khalji built the Hauz Khas tank around 1295 to supply Siri.
